title: Mediums substrate — StrokeProfile extraction + the high-quality painterly noise basis
headline: Build the substrate the W13 medium waves ride: (1) EXTRACT struct StrokeProfile + profileFor(medium, mode) + a single parameterized paintStrokeLayers(profile) from the 117-line mediumOil monolith (the per-mode if-ladder + the four hand-unrolled stroke layers collapse into a data table + one cascade — DRY substrate, byte-stable oil/knife/brushwork); (2) AUTHOR the NET-NEW Jarzynski PCG2D integer-bit hash + 2D simplex gradient-noise leaf (PCG_HASH_GLSL/PCG_HASH_WGSL) in the shared procedural-color chunk, single-sourced GLSL+WGSL twins under the OETF/FBM_ROT discipline, spliced into both aurora.frag.ts + aurora.wgsl.ts. Both changes VISUALLY NEUTRAL on the existing oil medium. SUBSTRATE wave — W13 authors profiles against it + opts the painterly mediums into the basis.

hashChoice.decision: Jarzynski PCG2D integer-bit hash (the canonical 'Hash Functions for GPU Rendering' JCGT 2020 pcg2d — two LCG mixes + an xor-shift fold per axis). PCG2D over PCG3D-collapsed-to-2D: PCG2D is the cheaper-correct default for a 2D field. Recorded default taken per Cadence §5.3 (orchestrator absent at impl; the spec's RECOMMENDED path).

gradientNoiseChoice.decision: 2D SIMPLEX gradient noise (Gustavson skew/unskew lattice; F2=(sqrt3-1)/2, G2=(3-sqrt3)/6, 70.0 amplitude normalize) seeded by pcg2d gradients. Simplex over classic-Perlin: patent-expired, lower directional-artifact default. Recorded default taken per Cadence §5.3 (the spec's RECOMMENDED path).

profileForHome.decision: struct StrokeProfile + profileFor + paintStrokeLayers ALL live in mediums.glsl.ts (the AURORA_MEDIUMS_POST_BRUSH_GLSL chunk, where the if-ladder + the four layers were). brush.glsl.ts is UNTOUCHED — bestOil/curvedStroke/paintOver/strokeShape stay the shared placement substrate the cascade CALLS (never re-authors). Rationale: the profile knobs are oil-medium data, co-located with the medium body; the brush SDFs are the cross-medium placement substrate. The spec allows either home; mediums.glsl.ts is the cleanest cohesion seam + keeps brush.glsl.ts out of bounds.

There is NO integer-PCG GLSL hash anywhere in src/, so no proof:aurora-noise-hash-equivalence gate can assert against anything.

folds.finding: slice 8 F6 — the mediumOil god-monolith / StrokeProfile-extraction root
folds.rootCause: mediumOil accreted four stroke modes + four stroke layers + crosshatch + tooth + relight in one function as each W4 fold landed serially on one worktree (the serial W4-fold accretion). The per-mode mode-selection is an imperative if-ladder (logic-as-branches); a new medium must edit the monolith, not author a profile.
folds.gestaltFix: Extracted struct StrokeProfile (the 12-field stroke-parameter cohort: shapeType/bristleAmp/streakFreq/streakAmp/impastoAmp/hardness/toothScale/toothAmp/pigmentSat/densityBig/densityMed/densitySml — logic-as-DATA, the if-ladder's knobs become fields) + profileFor(int medium, int mode) (the if-ladder folded into a data-table selector; a new medium adds a CASE, never edits a body) + a single parameterized void paintStrokeLayers(inout vec3 col, inout float height, StrokeProfile prof, int mode, vec2 p, float t) (the four hand-unrolled layers + crosshatch collapse into ONE cascade driven by the profile + the mode-invariant per-layer scale/anisotropy multipliers). mediumOil is now a thin body: profileFor(MEDIUM_OIL, mode) -> paintStrokeLayers -> tooth/relight/saturate finish reading the profile fields. The bestOil/curvedStroke/paintOver/strokeShape placement primitives in brush.glsl.ts STAY UNCHANGED — only the per-mode SELECTION moved from an imperative branch to a data table.
folds.evidence: mediums.glsl.ts: struct StrokeProfile (:222-233), StrokeProfile profileFor(int medium, int mode) (:239-275 — oil baseline ctor + mode==1 knife + mode==3 brushwork override blocks), void paintStrokeLayers(...) (:282-336 — the 4-layer + crosshatch cascade), mediumOil thin body (:338-369). #define MEDIUM_OIL 3 (:127). The extraction is byte/1e-6-NEUTRAL: tests/components/custom/aurora/mediums-extraction.test.ts (10 assertions) proves every if-ladder constant survived + the exact bestOil/paintOver call topology (offsets/seeds/multipliers) is preserved + the monolith if-ladder is gone from mediumOil.

folds.finding: slice 8 F4 — the value-noise/sin-hash fidelity-ceiling root
folds.rootCause: Every medium-texture term reads vnoise (value noise on the chained-fract hash21) / fbm / hash22 (fract(sin(p)*43758)). The characteristic blocky axis-aligned lattice + sin()-periodicity-banding read as 'digital procedural texture' — the wrong basis for organic paper/pigment grain the painterly mediums magnify. There is NO integer-PCG/gradient-noise leaf to opt into.
folds.gestaltFix: Authored the NET-NEW Jarzynski PCG2D integer-bit hash (pcg2d uvec2->uvec2) + a float->[0,1) scalar hash (pcgHash2 via floatBitsToUint+pcg2d) + an integer-lattice gradient (pcgGrad2) + 2D simplex gradient noise (gnoise) in the shared procedural-color.glsl.ts chunk as a GLSL twin (PCG_HASH_GLSL) + a WGSL twin (PCG_HASH_WGSL) — single-sourced under the same OETF/FBM_ROT two-twin discipline. Integer-bit kills the sin() periodicity-banding permanently; gradient noise kills the value-noise blocky lattice. Spliced ${PCG_HASH_GLSL} into aurora.frag.ts + ${PCG_HASH_WGSL} into aurora.wgsl.ts. The painterly mediums OPT INTO pcgHash2/gnoise; the smooth/atmospheric pole KEEPS its cheap value-noise fbm (the cost-tiering is preserved — this is an ADDITIVE basis, not a blanket upgrade). The aurora-local hash21/vnoise/fbm loop is NOT deleted (legitimately divergent per the chunk's §3a).
folds.evidence: procedural-color.glsl.ts: PCG_HASH_GLSL export (the pcg2d/pcgHash2/pcgGrad2/gnoise GLSL leaf) + PCG_HASH_WGSL twin + the // What lives here header inventory update. aurora.frag.ts: +PCG_HASH_GLSL import + ${PCG_HASH_GLSL} splice (after the fbm loop). aurora.wgsl.ts: +PCG_HASH_WGSL import + ${PCG_HASH_WGSL} splice (after the chunk color splices). The twin-equivalence is locked by proof:aurora-noise-hash-equivalence (numeric 1e-6 + structural splice-discipline).
